title: Calming Sleep-Sound Mixer — Claude model variant
description: A developer-operated Claude rerun of the canonical Calming Sleep-Sound Mixer brief, preserved as an auditable PathForge Labs model variant rather than a community fork.

comparison_basis.opening_prompt_exact: Build me a calming sleep-sound mixer I can save as one file and open in my browser. I want adjustable rain, fan, and brown-noise layers that are generated in the page instead of streamed, a few useful presets, and a sleep timer that fades out gently. It should feel reassuring and simple enough to use in the dark.
acceptance_criteria: Produce one complete self-contained HTML file.
Generate rain, fan, and brown-noise audio locally in the browser without streamed or bundled audio.
Provide independent layer controls plus a clearly labeled overall master-volume control.
Provide at least three genuinely distinct presets.
Provide a sleep timer with visible state, a gentle fade, and a truthful finished or cancelled state.
Start audio only from a user gesture and keep play, pause, and resume state truthful.
Operate offline with no external APIs, hosted generation, CDNs, remote fonts, scripts, stylesheets, or fragile dependencies.
Avoid unsafe HTML sinks, eval-like execution, inline event handlers, modal dialogs, and deprecated clipboard handling.
Avoid page-level horizontal overflow at 390 by 844 and at desktop width.
Keep essential controls visible and reachable while preserving exact prompt, response, and artifact evidence.
comparison_basis.adaptive_repair_policy: Preserve and score the first artifact. Continue only when verification proves a concrete defect or a source-capture failure; use the same source session and model; name the observed defect in ordinary language; preserve every real artifact version; stop as soon as the artifact passes; allow no more than three total prompts except for documented truncation or mechanical capture failure.
comparison_basis.independence_note: Claude received the invariant brief in a fresh session and was not shown the historical implementation, screenshots, source code, or another provider's output.

steps.title: Build the invariant sleep-sound mixer brief
steps.prompt_exact: Build me a calming sleep-sound mixer I can save as one file and open in my browser. I want adjustable rain, fan, and brown-noise layers that are generated in the page instead of streamed, a few useful presets, and a sleep timer that fades out gently. It should feel reassuring and simple enough to use in the dark.
steps.response_exact:
Caught a stray broken CSS line I left in — cleaning that up, then running your scanner checks.Here's Nightsound — one file, fully offline, everything synthesized in-page with the Web Audio API.

How the sound is made: rain is band-filtered white noise plus randomly scheduled droplet "plops" that scale with the slider; fan is low-passed noise with a shallow 5.3 Hz wobble and a faint 108 Hz motor hum underneath; brown noise is a leaky-integrator random walk through a soft lowpass. Sliders use a squared volume curve so the low end has fine control, which matters at 2 AM.

Usage details: hitting Play with everything at zero auto-loads Rainy Night so you never get silence, presets start playback immediately, and the sleep timer (15/30/45/60/90) counts down visibly and rolls into a 60-second exponential fade at the end — picking a new timer mid-fade ramps the volume back up. The moon breathes while playing (respects reduced-motion), and the whole UI is dim with 44px touch targets for dark-room use.

Your scans came back clean across the board: no innerHTML, no inline handlers, no modal APIs, no URL literals anywhere in the file, no letter-spacing, no vw/clamp font sizing, no external dependencies, no storage APIs. JS syntax-checked too.

One browser note: audio can't start without a user gesture, so the first tap on Play (or a preset) is what spins up the AudioContext — that's by design, not a bug.
steps.response_summary: Claude produced the first complete one-file Nightsound artifact.
steps.notes: Preserved as the unmodified first artifact. Verification found a missing overall-volume control, an abrupt pause path, and an Off-during-fade edge case.

steps.title: Repair the verified master, pause, and timer defects
steps.prompt_exact: I tested Nightsound. The three layer controls, playback, presets, timer UI, offline scan, and 390px layout are clean. One important mixer control is missing: there is no overall volume, so lowering the whole mix requires moving three sliders. Pause also suspends the AudioContext immediately instead of ramping down, which makes the manual stop abrupt. I also traced a timer edge case: choosing Off during the final fade clears the countdown but leaves the scheduled master fade active. Please add a clearly labeled master-volume slider, give Pause a short gentle ramp before suspension, and make Off cancel any scheduled fade and restore the chosen master level. Preserve every current feature and the offline one-file design, then return the complete updated HTML as the artifact.
steps.response_exact:
Good catches — all three are real. The fade fix needs a small architecture change: I'm splitting the master into an automation gain (play-in ramp, timer fade, pause ramp) and a separate user-controlled master gain, so timer fades and your master level never fight over the same node.Updated file above. What changed:

**Master volume.** New "Master volume" card sits below the three layers, styled like the others but with the moon accent so it reads as different in the dark. Defaults to 100% so existing behavior is unchanged, uses the same squared perceptual curve as the layer sliders. Under the hood the signal chain is now `layers → master (automation) → masterVol (your slider) → destination`, so the timer fade, play-in ramp, and pause ramp all operate on a separate node and never clobber your chosen level — and vice versa.

**Gentle pause.** Pause now does a 0.5s exponential ramp to silence, then suspends the context ~100ms after the ramp lands. If you hit Play again during that window, the pending suspend is cancelled cleanly and playback ramps back in.

**Off cancels the fade.** Choosing Off mid-fade now cancels all scheduled values on the automation gain and ramps it back to full over 2 seconds, so the mix recovers to exactly the master level you had set. The existing "picked a new timer mid-fade" recovery path got the same benefit for free since it also targets the automation gain.

Your full scan suite is still clean (no innerHTML, inline handlers, modal APIs, URL literals, letter-spacing, vw/clamp fonts, external deps, or storage), JS syntax-checked, and everything else — presets, droplet scheduler, timer countdown, auto-preset on silent play — is untouched.
steps.response_summary: Claude repaired the measured mixer-state defects and returned the complete updated artifact.
steps.continuation_reason: Verification-proven defects: missing overall volume, immediate pause suspension, and scheduled fade persisting after Off.
steps.notes: Final verified production artifact. No additional continuation was warranted.
